_notes: Planet surfaces for the game prototype (game/): a hex grid on 3D terrain. The game starts in orbit: the scan shows terrain and rough deposit hints per region; the player picks a landing site, the colony pod descends, and survey rovers reveal exact deposits as they drive. terrain: move_cost = effort to enter a tile (unit speed is effort per second); height = visual relief level. planets: per planet class, how a surface is generated. Elevation and moisture come from deterministic noise (feature_size = tiles per noise cell) and are ranked, so thresholds are shares of the map: elevation ocean 0.30 = the lowest 30% of tiles are ocean, below shallows = shallows, from hills up = hills, from mountains up = mountains, the rest is lowland; within lowland, moisture picks the terrain; polar_rows at top and bottom become polar_terrain. deposits: rolled per tile on matching terrain (coastal = must touch water); amounts are ranges. hints: region totals below likely = traces, below rich = likely, otherwise rich. landing: where a colony pod may set down (tile terrain, and every neighbour must be passable land), how long it falls, what it brings (start_stock, the hub building, units) and how far the landing reveals; assemble_seconds = how long the landed Colony Hub (and every outpost dropped from orbit) takes to assemble after touchdown: it stands on its tile but gives no output, power, storage, build range, build queues or repair pad until then (the vehicles can drive at once). build_menu: buildings the player can place on the surface (their costs and stats are in buildings.json: build_seconds, output_per_min, upkeep_per_min, extract_per_min, requires_deposit; the hub's build_radius and build_queues limit where and how many build at once). Tiles must be surveyed and buildable to build on. Power: power_resource (energy) is not stockpiled on a surface; each base (a colony core and the buildings in its radius) has a power budget: power_supply of its working buildings vs power_use; when use exceeds supply, every power user at that base runs at supply/use speed. Levels: a core upgrades along upgrades_to (Colony Hub 1 → Colonial Administration 2 → Planetary Capital 3), paying the next level's cost and taking its build_seconds; it keeps working meanwhile. Storage: stockpiled materials (everything except storage_exempt) share one capacity per player, the sum of storage on their finished buildings (the hub's vault, Storage Containers, refineries); mining stops when it is full. Hills and plains hold raw ore, which an Ore Refinery turns into metal: duranium ore lies in hills and plains (plains are landing ground, so a mine near the hub usually finds some), tritanium ore only in hills (often a crawler drive away); duranium is needed about three times as much (economy retune 2026-11-07, balance/README.md). salvage_refund: share of the cost returned when a finished building is salvaged. units: speed = move effort per second; mark = which mark of a vehicle line it is (1-3: survey_rover is the Mk I Scout, survey_rover_mk2 the Mk II Surveyor, survey_rover_mk3 the Mk III Explorer); cost and build_seconds = what a Vehicle Bay charges and takes to assemble one; a unit with extract_per_min is a mining crawler: it unfurls on a deposit (deploy_seconds), fills a hopper and sends each full load home as a cargo pod that flies pod_speed tiles per second to the nearest storage building or refinery. breakdown: while mining, each minute has chance_per_min of a breakdown; the severity is picked by weight and knocks damage (a range) off its integrity (100 = perfect); an explosion also loses the load in the hopper. A broken crawler folds up, can't mine, and drives slower (down to slowest_drive of its speed at 0 integrity). repair: drive it onto a colony core's tile (the repair pad beside the hub); after crew_seconds (the repair crew walking out) the crew take the spare kits the repair needs (fabrication.json: one of the unit's kit per kit_points integrity missing, rounded up, plus breakdown_kits for a broken-down crawler; with too few in stock it waits for them, or the player jury-rigs it) and it regains per_second integrity until it is back to 100. damage (survey rovers): while driving, each terrain wears wear integrity a minute and has a hazard chance a minute (one of the hazards listed for that terrain, picked by weight, knocks damage off; a hazard with flat also punctures a tyre) and a flat chance a minute; a toxic tile corrodes toxic_per_min wherever the rover is, and on a predator tile wildlife attacks with chance_per_min (damage range); research with the breakdown stat scales the hazard and flat chances. found (the construction rover): founding a second outpost on the ground. The rover drives to a surveyed, buildable tile that is safe (no toxic ground, predators or native land), has no building on it or next to it and is at least min_distance tiles from the player's other colony cores (and from an outpost on its way down), parks and unfolds over deploy_seconds (paying cost as it starts; a move order folds it back up and refunds it), then is used up: building (a colony core) stands on the tile as a new base under construction, built by exocomps over that building's build_seconds in buildings.json using a build queue of its own; cancelling it before it is finished refunds cost and the rover rolls back out. min_distance is shorter than orbit outpost_drop.min_distance (8 vs 10: two Colony Hub build radii of 4, so the build areas never overlap) and the cost is lower than a drop (no drop ships; the panels come from the Vehicle Bay with the rover, and its crew drive over). Below slow_below integrity it drives slower, down to slowest_drive of its speed at 0; below sensors_below its survey radius drops by sensor_loss (at least 1); at 0 it is disabled: it stops, surveys nothing and only a repair order moves it, at crawl (also the slowest it ever drives). tyres: wheels (4 or 6; bit order front left, front right, [middle left, middle right,] rear left, rear right) and spares carried; the flat chance rises by low_integrity times the share of integrity lost; one flat drives at flat_speed, two or more at two_flat_speed, and each flat adds flat_wear (a share) to the terrain wear; the crew change a flat in the field in change_seconds parked (uses a spare, a move order stops it); a repair pad (crew_seconds walk, then) fits a new tyre on every flat and restocks the spares (fabrication.json pad_tyre_kits of pad_tyre_kit a tyre, taken with the repair's other kits), then welds integrity back as for the crawler (repair). Any vehicle parked on its own colony core's pad that needs it is repaired. maintenance: buildings with wear_per_min lose that much condition (0..100) a minute while they work; below decline_below their output falls toward slowest_output at 0, and each minute they may break down outright (chance rising to break_chance_per_min_at_zero at 0); a broken building stops until maintained. Manual maintenance: the base's crew walks out (crew_walk_seconds + crew_seconds_per_tile per tile from the core), one job at a time per base, and restores repair_per_second once it has taken the spare kits the repair needs (fabrication.json: the building's kit, one per kit_points condition missing, rounded up; with too few in stock the crew wait, or the player jury-rigs it); buildings with auto_maintain (a top level, or the Automated Maintenance tech) fix themselves with drones whenever they drop below auto_below. research: surface techs a Research Lab works on (cost in research points; requires = techs needed first); modifiers add to building stats (speed, yield, wear) for the listed buildings (all buildings when none are listed), auto_maintain turns on drones, breakdown scales a unit's breakdown chance; ids shared with tech_tree.json are the same tech (deep_core_mining). orbit: the player's ship over the planet (name and ships.json class per faction), its cargo hold, and ways down: outpost_drop (a new Colony Hub at a safe site at least min_distance tiles from your other cores, after the first landing), shuttle (the drop ship: flies a payload unit down to a safe tile and goes back up), satellite (orbits over a band of band_rows rows and sweeps it every sweep_seconds, surveying it), transporter (levels by era, overridden per faction; range = tiles from your nearest base or unit, 0 = anywhere; cargo = supplies from the hold per beam; cooldown between beams). hud_resources: the stockpiled resources shown in the top bar, in order. unit_names: every new unit (landed, delivered or built) gets a name from pool and a number from the numbers range, in a random-looking order from the map seed; a player never gets the same name or number twice (when the pool runs out names go on as NAME II, NAME III...; when the numbers run out they go on with three digits). environments: per planet class, what the outpost's sensors read once its uplink to the ship is online (landing.assemble_seconds after touchdown): sky = the colour of the sky in the helm's surface feed; gravity_g; day_hours = the local day as shown on the clock, day_seconds = how long it lasts in game time; relief_km = altitude of the highest ground (land altitude rises with the cube of its elevation share above the ocean); temperature_c day/night = equator, sea-level afternoon high and pre-dawn low, polar_drop = how much colder the map's top and bottom rows are (rising with the square of the latitude), lapse_per_km = cooling with altitude; humidity_pct = the driest and wettest relative humidity (a tile's wetness from its terrain, biomass and water nearby picks within it, higher at night); wind_ms mean and gust; pressure_kpa at sea level, falling with altitude over scale_height_km (0 = no atmosphere); radiation_usv_h = surface dose rate in µSv/h by day and night (more at altitude and toward the poles); uv_index at noon; atmosphere_pct = the main gases, summing to 100 (empty for a vacuum); trace_ppm = trace gases; toxic_ppm = what a toxic patch (the biologics scan) adds to the air on it, fading over three tiles. telemetry: exposure_limits_ppm per gas (readings above it are flagged as hazards), breathable_o2_pct and breathable_kpa (outside = unbreathable), radiation, heat, cold and gust warning levels, and per terrain how much it scales the day/night temperature swing (swing), shifts the temperature (offset_c) and scales the humidity and the wind. Readings are pure functions of the data, the map, the tile and the tick (no dice rolls): a day/night cycle by the tile's longitude, slow weather noise and gusts. lanes: how vehicles drive inside the hexes (world units; a hex is 25 across, 12.5 from its centre to an edge). A vehicle goes from tile to tile through the shared edge, crossing it lane_offset to the right of its direction of travel (so opposite traffic passes), and its time per world unit on a tile is that tile's move_cost / 25 (so a tile still costs about its move_cost). On a tile with a building (its buildings.json footprint_radius, else default_footprint), a deployed or unfolding vehicle (units' footprint_radius: a crawler's rig, a construction rover's site) it bends round the centre on a ring footprint + clearance out. A vehicle ordered onto a tile parks at a spot of its own: a building's access point, else the centre, else one of six spots toward the corners (park_radius out on an empty tile, 12.5 out beside a building), the free one nearest where it came in; a group ordered onto one tile fills its spots and the rest park on the tiles round it. Paths cost 1 more through a tile with a building or a deployed vehicle (not the goal), so traffic goes round bases when that is about as quick. It swerves round vehicles parked on its tile (avoid_radius) and waits while another vehicle is less than gap_ahead in front of it and less than gap_side to the side; after wait_seconds it drives on regardless for push_seconds (so nothing deadlocks). All numbers are placeholders.
